I suggest trying this: - https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/discussions/2377 It not only supports syntax highlighting, but is also more flexible and supports alignment as well. ### Related - https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/discussions/2151 - https://github.com/folke/snacks.nvim/blob/main/lua/snacks/picker/util/highlight.lua ### Similar - https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/discussions/988 - https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/discussions/1192 ### Example ### Known issues > [!WARNING] > 1. ~~Blinking highlights.~~ This is a known Neovim issue that occurs when multiple highlights share the same range. > See https://github.com/neovim/neovim/discussions/37020. > > *Solved by incrementing the priority by one each time the same column highlight appears.* > Highlight display may look different from the buffer. > > 2. Some keywords may not be highlighted correctly. This happens because language-specific treesitter may not highlight incomplete keywords, such as `for do` without a corresponding `end` in Lua (see `get_text_patched_highlights`). It’s **not** the case for the `buf_lines`, `hipatterns` pickers since they get their highlights directly from the buffer (see `get_buf_highlights`). ### Code

".so", false) or not vim.api.nvim_get_runtime_file("queries/" .. lang .. "/highlights.scm", false) then return {} end -- Create scratch buffer local buf = lang_bufs[lang] if not (buf and vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(buf)) then ---@cast buf integer buf = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true) lang_bufs[lang] = buf end -- vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(buf, 0, -1, false, vim.split(code, "\n", { plain = true })) vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(buf, 0, -1, false, code) -- Init parser local parser = vim.treesitter.get_parser(buf, lang, { error = false }) if not parser then return {} end parser:parse(true) -- Get highlights (copy-paste from snacks.nvim) local ret = {} parser:for_each_tree(function(tstree, tree) if not tstree then return end local query = vim.treesitter.query.get(tree:lang(), "highlights") if not query then return end for capture, node, metadata in query:iter_captures(tstree:root(), buf) do ---@type string local name = query.captures[capture] if name ~= "spell" then local range = { node:range() } ---@type number[] local multi = range[1] ~= range[3] local text = multi and vim.split(vim.treesitter.get_node_text(node, buf, metadata[capture]), "\n", { plain = true }) or {} for row = range[1] + 1, range[3] + 1 do local first, last = row == range[1] + 1, row == range[3] + 1 local end_col = last and range[4] or #(text[row - range[1]] or "") end_col = multi and first and end_col + range[2] or end_col ret[row] = ret[row] or {} table.insert(ret[row], { col = first and range[2] or 0, end_col = end_col, priority = (tonumber(metadata.priority or metadata[capture] and metadata[capture].priority) or 100), conceal = metadata.conceal or metadata[capture] and metadata[capture].conceal, hl_group = "@" .. name .. "." .. lang, }) end end end end) return ret end -- Show function local grep_cache = {} -- Clear cache vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("User", { pattern = "MiniPickStop", callback = function() grep_cache = {} end, }) local grep_ns = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace("minipick_grep") local minipick_grep_show = function(buf, data, query, opts) -- Clear previous highlights vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf, grep_ns, 0, -1) -- Default show MiniPick.default_show(buf, data, query, opts) -- Highlight code local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf, 0, -1, true) for ln in ipairs(data) do -- Parse local line = lines[ln] local file, file_row, file_col, code = unpack(vim.split(data[ln], "%z")) local ft = vim.filetype.match({ filename = file }) or "" -- Get highlights +cache local cache_id = string.format("%s|%s|%s", file, file_row, file_col) local line_hls = grep_cache[cache_id] if not line_hls then line_hls = get_code_highlights({ code }, ft)[1] grep_cache[cache_id] = line_hls end -- Apply highlights if line_hls then -- NOTE: Prevent cache mutation line_hls = vim.deepcopy(line_hls, true) -- Find code start local _, off = string.find(line, ".*│.*│.*│") -- Set extmarks local extm_row = ln - 1 for _, hl in ipairs(line_hls) do local extm_col = off + hl.col hl.col = nil hl.end_col = off + hl.end_col local ok, err = pcall(vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark, buf, grep_ns, extm_row, extm_col, hl) if not ok then vim.notify("Set extmark: " .. err, vim.log.levels.WARN) end end end end end vim.api.nvim_set_hl(0, "MiniPickMatchRanges", { bold = true, underdotted = true, }) -- Set `source.show` for grep pickers MiniPick.registry.grep = function(local_opts, opts) return MiniPick.builtin.grep( local_opts, vim.tbl_deep_extend("keep", opts or {}, { source = { show = minipick_grep_show } }) ) end MiniPick.registry.grep_live = function(local_opts, opts) return MiniPick.builtin.grep_live( local_opts, vim.tbl_deep_extend("keep", opts or {}, { source = { show = minipick_grep_show } }) ) end ```

1 local col_0 = #info buf_set_highlights(buf, minipick_hl_ns, row_0, col_0, line_hls) end end -- -- Buffer lines local minipick_buf_lines_show = function(buf, data, query, opts) vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf, minipick_hl_ns, 0, -1) MiniPick.default_show(buf, data, query, opts) -- Syntax highlight local bufs = {} for _, item in ipairs(data) do bufs[item.bufnr] = true end local buf_hls = {} for item_buf in pairs(bufs) do buf_hls[item_buf] = minipick_use_cache(item_buf, function() local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(item_buf, 0, -1, true) return get_code_highlights(lines, vim.bo[item_buf].ft) end) end local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf, 0, #data, true) for ln, item in ipairs(data) do local line = lines[ln] local item_buf, lnum = item.bufnr, item.lnum local line_hls = buf_hls[item_buf][lnum] or {} local row_0 = ln -       if add then
        table.insert(lines, 1, add)

    for _, word in ipairs(vim.split(last, "%s+")) do
      local add = append[word]
      if add then
        table.insert(lines, add)
      end
    end

end
-- HACK: `MiniPick.default_show` replaces tabs (\t) with spaces,
-- so we shift the highlights accordingly
local get_buf_lnum_hls = function(buf, with_extmarks, lnum)
  local line = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf, lnum - 1, lnum, true)[1]
  local hls = get_buf_highlights(buf, with_extmarks, { lnum - 1, lnum })
  local tab_offset = function(col)
    local _, t_count = line:sub(1, col):gsub("\t", "")
    return t_count * (vim.o.tabstop - 1)
  end
  for _, row_hls in ipairs(hls) do
    for _, hl in ipairs(row_hls) do
      if hl.col then
        hl.col = hl.col + tab_offset(hl.col)
      end
      if hl.end_col then
        hl.end_col = hl.end_col + tab_offset(hl.end_col)
      end
    end
  end
  return hls
end
-- Setup
local minipick_hl_ns = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace("minipick_hl")
local pick_colorize = function(buf, data, get_hls)
  vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf, minipick_hl_ns, 0, -1)
  local lines = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(buf, 0, -1, true)
  for i = 1, #data do
    local item, line = data[i], lines[i]
    local start, hls = get_hls(item, line)
    if start and hls and not vim.tbl_isempty(hls) then
      local row_start, col_offset = i - 1, start - 1
      -- NOTE: To prevent cache changes
      hls = vim.deepcopy(hls, true)
      for j, row_hls in ipairs(hls) do
        local row = row_start + j - 1
        for _, hl in ipairs(row_hls) do
          vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark(buf, minipick_hl_ns, norm_hl(hl, row, col_offset))

      end
    end

end
local minipick_cache = {}
local pick_cache = function(id, func)
  if not vim.list_contains({ "string", "number" }, type(id)) then
    error("Cache 'id' must be 'string' or 'number'")
  end
  if minipick_cache[id] == nil then
    minipick_cache[id] = { func() }
  end
  return unpack(minipick_cache[id])
end
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("User", {
  pattern = "MiniPickStop",
  callback = function()

  end,
})

MiniPick.registry.buf_lines = function(local_opts, opts)
  local find_pattern = local_opts.scope == "all" and "^.-│.-│()" or "^.-│()"
  local show = function(buf, data, query)
    MiniPick.default_show(buf, data, query, opts)
    pick_colorize(buf, data, function(item, line)
      local item_buf, row = item.bufnr, item.lnum
      local id = vim.inspect({ item_buf, row })
      return pick_cache(id, function()
        local start = string.match(line, find_pattern)
        local hls = get_buf_lnum_hls(item_buf, true, row)
        return start, hls
      end)
    end)
  end
  opts = vim.tbl_deep_extend("keep", opts or {}, { source = { show = show } })

end

  local show = function(buf, data, query)
    MiniPick.default_show(buf, data, query, opts)
    pick_colorize(buf, data, function(item, line)
      local id, start, code = string.match(line, "^(.-│.-│)()(.*)")
      return pick_cache(id, function()
        local file = item.path
        local ft = vim.filetype.match({ filename = file, contents = { code } })
        return start, get_text_patched_highlights(code, ft)
      end)
    end)
  end
  opts = vim.tbl_deep_extend("keep", opts or {}, { source = { show = show } })
  return MiniExtra.pickers.git_hunks(local_opts, opts)
end
local grep_show = function(buf, data, query, opts)
  opts = opts or {}
  MiniPick.default_show(buf, data, query, opts)
  pick_colorize(buf, data, function(item, line)
    local file, row, col, code = unpack(vim.split(item, "%z"))
    local id = vim.inspect({ file, row, col })
    return pick_cache(id, function()
      local start = string.match(line, "^.-│.-│.-│()")

end

  opts = vim.tbl_deep_extend("keep", opts or {}, { source = { show = grep_show } })

end
MiniPick.registry.grep_live = function(local_opts, opts)
  opts = vim.tbl_deep_extend("keep", opts or {}, { source = { show = grep_show } })
  return MiniPick.builtin.grep_live(local_opts, opts)
end
MiniPick.registry.hipatterns = function(local_opts, opts)
  local show = function(buf, data, query)
    MiniPick.default_show(buf, data, query, opts)
    pick_colorize(buf, data, function(item, line)
      local item_buf, row, col = item.bufnr, item.lnum, item.col

      return pick_cache(id, function()
        local start = string.match(line, "^.-│.-│.-│.-│()")

MiniPick.registry.history = function(local_opts, opts)
  local show = function(buf, data, query)
    MiniPick.default_show(buf, data, query, opts)
    pick_colorize(buf, data, function(item, line)
      local id = item
      return pick_cache(id, function()
        local start = string.match(line, "^: ()")
        if start then

end

  local find_pattern = local_opts.scope == "document_symbol" and "^.-%[.-%]()(.*)" or "^.-│.-│.-│()(.*)"
  local show = function(buf, data, query)
    MiniPick.default_show(buf, data, query, opts)
    pick_colorize(buf, data, function(item, line)
      local file, row, col = item.path, item.lnum, item.col

      return pick_cache(id, function()
        local start, code = string.match(line, find_pattern)

I reworked the code a bit, but it was pretty hard. Now I understand why this feature is too rough to add to the *mini.nvim* ecosystem.

There are a few problems, which I described in the **Known Issues** section:

1. Some parsers (e.g. Lua) do not highlight incomplete keywords, which is the real problem, since external tools usually print output as a single line. In this case, regex-based highlighting might even work better.
**NOTE**: This does not apply to the `buf_lines` picker, since it gets highlighting directly from the buffer.

2. Highlighting may blink like crazy while you're typing or moving the cursor. As far as I understand, this happens because Neovim does not guarantee the order in which highlights with the same range (the same column start) are applied, even when the third-party highlight have a different priority. I guess this can be overcome by regrouping the highlights or applying them all at once, though I haven't tried it. See https://github.com/neovim/neovim/discussions/37020.

comment_data.body:
Syntax/treesitter highlighting in a fuzzy picker is technically interesting — the challenge is that you're rendering small excerpts of files, not full buffers, so you can't just attach a treesitter parser to a "file" in the normal sense.

**The approaches**:

**1. Buffer-based highlighting (what most pickers do)**
Create a scratch buffer, set the filetype, put the content in. Treesitter attaches automatically if a grammar is installed. The downside: creating/destroying buffers for 10k+ matches is expensive.

**2. Pre-cached highlight regions**
Use the treesitter API to get highlight captures for a file and cache them. When the picker shows a preview, look up the cached captures and apply them directly as extmarks. The file parsing happens once; rendering the picker just applies pre-computed highlight data.

**3. Highlight on-demand for visible items only**
Only treesitter-highlight the items currently visible in the picker window. As the user scrolls or narrows the search, compute highlights for the new visible set. This bounds the work to a constant (visible window height) rather than O(all matches).

**4. Async highlighting**
Highlight matches in the background as the user interacts. The picker renders without highlights first (fast), then updates highlights as they're computed. Gives responsiveness without blocking on highlighting.

The 350 LOC constraint is interesting — approach 3 or 4 would be the most practical to implement concisely while still delivering good UX for the common case (user has narrowed to a small candidate set).

Is the goal highlighting in the picker list itself (each line), in the preview window, or both?
